items.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 13 at 4:20PM PDT until October 15 at 2:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
items.description:
* WHAT...Minor tidal overflow during times of high tides,
dangerous rip currents, and elevated surf.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles
County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding of sea water is likely around high
tide at low-lying beach and harbor areas that is uncommon with
normal tidal ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is possible. The
risk for significant damage is very low. There is an increased
risk of ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and
surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor tidal overflow during morning high
tides of 6.5 to 7.0 feet.
items.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

items.headline: Heat Advisory issued October 13 at 11:21AM PDT until October 17 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
items.description:
* WHAT...Temperatures up to 95 expected.

* WHERE...Los Angeles County Beaches, Los Angeles County Inland Coast
including Downtown Los Angeles, Palos Verdes Hills, San Luis Obispo
County Beaches, San Luis Obispo County Inland Central Coast, Santa
Barbara County Central Coast Beaches, Santa Barbara County Inland
Central Coast, Santa Barbara County Southeastern Coast, and Santa
Barbara County Southwestern Coast.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Thursday to 8 PM PDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses.
items.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

In the event of a nearby wildfire, smoke may increase heat and
physical stress. If smoke impacts your area; 1) Have a cooling plan
in place as smoke could limit your ability to cool your home through
open windows and 2) If you have air conditioning, set on air
recirculation within the home to avoid smoke exposure. Local
officials may have additional guidance.
